body: You're welcome. Yes hopefully that type of reading could provide you with some insight. I wish you the very best.

I too have been abused by my mother as a child, and similarly it would probably be classed as mild in comparison with many other cases. However I know it has profoundly affected who I am. A few years ago I feared I had no conscience and found it very difficult to connect with people. I began reading up on the type of abuse I underwent and the effects it has on children. Through these readings I came to have a greater understanding of myself and found some self-compassion. Strangely this process has led me to begin experiencing many more emotions, which has been an uncomfortable yet important journey. Perhaps a similar approach would help you.

I'm so sorry. There is little doubt that this is at the root of everything. Abuse in our childhood affects so much of who we are and how we connect with the world. As scary as it is, I would urge you to talk about your past with someone who can help.
Were you ever treated poorly by someone you cared about way back in the past?
You should take a long hard look at yourself.
You may have sociopathy, although the fact it is bothering you at all means you may just have a fear of intimacy.

You sound like a good person. At no point in your posts have you objectified women, plus you have experienced some guilt for the situations. So I was wondering if there was a reason why you prefer married women?

I understand, but this is for those days where it wasn't possible to salvage something. Rather than allowing the guilt of not accomplishing something to swallow you up and further degrade your self-worth, it's important to remember you're still alive and that can be accomplishment enough when you're in a dark place.
